newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton dealers demand free exchange rate.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton dealers demand free exchange rate.

text.p: Pakistan cotton dealers on Monday demanded a free exchange rate of the rupee on trade accounts to increase exports.
A free exchange rate would boost cotton export, Maqbool Sadiq, the outgoing chairman of the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA), told the 64th general body meeting of the KCA.

"In order to boost exports, I further suggest that a free exchange rate policy on trade accounts may be followed under which exporters may be allowed to receive export proceeds at market rate, as determined by the free market mechanism and not at the fixed exchange rate as is the case at present," he said.
Registration of cotton export contracts had plunged to 27,313 375-lb bales by February 24, compared with 2.112 million in the year-ago period, broker Nasim Usman said.

Usman attributed this to a sharp decline in cotton production, estimated at 8.75 million in 1996/97 (July-June), against about 9.94 million in 1995/96, and to higher prices in the domestic markets due to the imposition of sales tax.
Sadiq said the crop in Punjab had been set back by pests, disease and frost.
